title: Glacial interchange ran mainly north to south because northern forms were more dominant

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Glacial interchange ran mainly north to south because northern forms were more dominant

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Many more identical and allied plant forms migrated from north to south during the Glacial period than in the reverse direction, because the greater land area of the north and the larger populations there had made northern forms more advanced and dominant through natural selection and competition.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I suspect that this preponderant migration from north to south is due to the greater extent of land in the north, and to the northern forms having existed in their own homes in greater numbers, and having consequently been advanced through natural selection and competition to a higher stage of perfection or dominating power, than the southern forms.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XI, “Geographical Distribution”; section “Dispersal during the Glacial period co-extensive with the world”. Scope: plants migrating between hemispheres during the Glacial period

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch11-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Migration asymmetry is testable, but Darwin's population-size and competitive-superiority mechanism requires uncertain proxies. Existing data can resolve parts of the causal chain rather than the full explanation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Infer direction and counts of cross-equatorial plant migrations through time, then model whether northern land area, inferred source population size, and competitive traits predict southward establishment. Support requires a north-to-south excess mediated by those proposed variables.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Glacial genomic sampling is sparse in the southern hemisphere.

Migration direction and extinction can be confounded.

'Dominating power' has no direct common measure.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.52
data adequacy: 0.47
data existence: 0.73
operationalizability: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A predominance of north-to-south events is inferable for clades that already have trees and range data, which is a subset of southern disjunct plants. The selective-dominance explanation is an extra causal claim those reconstructions do not decide. Compilation and sensitivity to sampling keep the directional test partial.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For plant clades disjunct between the hemispheres, infer dispersal direction from ancestral-area reconstruction and test whether north-to-south events predominate. Counts of direction do not by themselves show that natural selection on a larger northern land area caused the asymmetry.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Direction of spread does not measure dominating power or demonstrate selection.

Ancestral-area results move when extinction or northern sampling bias is modeled differently.

Amphitropical clades have been studied one at a time and are not one analysis-ready table.
